bfs-order.why: BFS visits by distance: 0, then its neighbours 1 and 2, then 3 (queued once, by 1, and skipped when 2 finds it already seen).

dfs-order.why: DFS goes as deep as it can first: 0, then 1, then 1's neighbour 3. It backs up to 0 and visits 2, whose neighbour 3 is already seen.

mark-when-queued.why: Marking on enqueue guarantees each node enters the queue once, which keeps BFS at O(V + E).

bfs-cost.why: Each vertex is dequeued once and each adjacency list is scanned once.

islands.why: Each flood fill marks one whole island, and every cell is visited once: O(rows × columns). Union-find also works with a bit more machinery.

bfs-steps.why: Seed the queue with the start, then repeatedly take the front node and queue its unseen neighbours until nothing is left.
